prompt: A mono blue stompy prison deck in Premodern that also uses Extravagant Spirit

results.prompt: A mono blue stompy prison deck in Premodern that also uses Extravagant Spirit
results.text:
I built **Mono-Blue Orb Stompy**, a brew with Extravagant Spirit as the main threat. The deck passed the legality check and was accepted.

**The plan:** The prison pieces are Winter Orb, Rishadan Port, Tangle Wire, Wasteland, Daze and Force Spike. They keep the opponent on about one land per turn. Meanwhile we empty our hand on a curve that averages 1.79 mana. That matters because Extravagant Spirit says "sacrifice this creature unless you pay {1} for each card in your hand." With the hand nearly empty, the upkeep costs 0–1 mana and the Spirit is a cheap 4/4 flier that ends the game.

**Why each piece is there:**
- **Mox Diamond:** gets a land out of our hand and gives blue mana that Winter Orb can't lock.
- **Cloud of Faeries:** costs nothing under Orb because it untaps two lands.
- **Waterfront Bouncer:** discards extra cards to keep the Spirit's upkeep at zero, and bounces blockers.
- **Stifle and Phyrexian Dreadnought:** a backup kill borrowed from the Stiflenought deck on the menu. Stifle stops Dreadnought's sacrifice trigger, leaving you a 12/12 trampler. Stifle can also counter fetch lands, Wasteland, or our own Spirit or Tangle Wire upkeep triggers.

**The three directions I considered:**
1. A Winter Orb fliers deck plus the Stiflenought Dreadnought/Stifle package.
2. Mono-Blue Merfolk with Orb (Lord of Atlantis, Looter) and the Spirit on top.
3. A Stasis lock using the Spirit as the finisher.

I chose the first. Its cheap, near-free spells empty the hand fastest, which is what the Spirit needs. Merfolk Looter draws and discards, so it never shrinks the hand. Stasis stops you from untapping, so you'd have no mana to pay the Spirit's upkeep.

**Honest odds:**
- You'll see at least one Spirit by turn 4 in about 53% of games.
- You'll have both Dreadnought and Stifle by turn 4 in only about 26%, so Dreadnought is a backup plan, not the main one.
- The checker says you'll have drawn every card in my full 7-card sample line by turn 7 in only 1.4% of games. That number is low because it requires all seven specific cards. The real kill only needs a Spirit or another flier, an Orb, and a mostly empty hand.

**Assumptions:**
- I read "stompy prison" as mana denial plus cheap threats.
- 17 lands is fewer than the checker recommends (21.4), but it matches real Orb tempo decks. The Merfolk lists average 18 lands, and Mox Diamond and Cloud of Faeries make up the difference.
- The 15-card sideboard is aimed at red decks, green decks, graveyard decks and artifact/enchantment decks from the current field.

deck.donor: Merfolk (Winter Orb mono-blue tempo) with the Stiflenought Dreadnought/Stifle package

winLine.does: Turn 1: pitch a spare land (one card out of hand) for a blue source Winter Orb can't lock
Turn 1-2: the prison; opponents untap one land a turn while our curve sits at 0-2 mana
Free under Orb: untaps two lands, adds a flying body and gets one more card out of our hand
Taps the opponent's single untapped land on their upkeep so they stay locked
Turn 3-4: a 4/4 flier; with our hand near empty the upkeep cost is 0-1, so it is a cheap 4-power clock
Discards our extra cards to keep the hand (and Spirit's tax) at zero while bouncing blockers
Protects the lock (fetches, Spirit/Tangle Wire triggers) or turns Phyrexian Dreadnought into a 12/12 backup finisher

needs.role: Empty the hand fast so the upkeep tax is 0-1 mana: cheap/free spells and discard outlets that dump cards
Mana that ignores Winter Orb to cast the 4-drop and pay any leftover upkeep

partnerHints.message: Phyrexian Dreadnought: 97% of the 325 premodern lists that run it are Stiflenought, and 99% play it alongside Vision Charm, which this deck doesn't have. It's usually there for a job that needs Vision Charm. Cut it, or say what it does here.
